discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 240639
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
139 AM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Increasing clouds today which stick around through at least
  Friday. High temperatures will be in the 40s this week.

- A period of soaking rain arrives early Thursday morning and
  lingers through Friday (80-90% chance). A few snowflakes may
  mix in Thursday night. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 133 AM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

High pressure over Minnesota seeps east through today and is 
currently working to disrupt meager lake-effect returns over far 
southeast Lake Michigan. A steady does of lake effect clouds this 
morning are favored to mix out from east to west this morning, 
through plenty of high clouds are noted just west of the Mississippi 
River. As a result, increasing clouds today which locks in 
temperatures near 40. 

A pair of upper-level troughs are noted on water vapor; one over the 
Alberta-Saskakutchan line and the second digging through the Four 
Corners. These two features track east through time and eventually 
lift northeast late this week. An overall dearth of cold air leaves 
local precipitation Wednesday night through Friday to be primary 
rain. However, those with travel interest over central IL should 
note light snowfall there Wednesday night. This remains a rather odd 
setup and evolution with two cyclones in close proximity 
absolutely soaking up Atlantic moisture and spilling it into the 
Midwest. If there are any snowflakes locally, Thursday night may be 
the "best" opportunity as the eastern most surface low occludes and 
northeasterly fetch through interior Canada promotes somewhat improved 
cold air advection. Overall, a prolonged period of soaking rain 
early Thursday morning through Friday. Rain will generally total 
0.50 to 0.75", with lower amounts over Michiana and greater amounts 
toward Muncie and Lima, OH. 

Northwest flow through the remainder of the weekend may permit 
another disturbance to pass through, yet run-to-run consistency has 
been poor so far. What continues to be advertised is a return to 
zonal flow or perhaps even uper-levle riding to begin December. This 
would bring us back toward above-normal temperatures. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1222 AM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

Increased mid level ridging and subsidence takes over behind today's 
trough alluding to reduced chances for precipitation. Surface high 
pressure traverses the area and this keeps flight conditions in VFR 
through the period. Initially north winds become more east winds as 
the surface high traverses eastward on a track through the north of 
the area. This evolution also keeps speeds below 10 kts through the 
period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 7 AM EST this morning for LMZ043-
     046.

&&

$$

spc.text:
SPC AC 240528

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1128 PM CST Mon Nov 23 2026

   Valid 241200Z - 251200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated thunderstorms are possible over parts of western/southern
   Texas, the Gulf Coast, Florida, and the West Coast today. Severe
   storms are unlikely.

   ...Synopsis...
   Severe thunderstorm potential is expected to remain limited across
   the country for today and tonight. Late-evening water-vapor imagery
   depicts a progressive upper wave moving out of the Four Corners
   region and into the southern High Plains. This feature will continue
   eastward towards the lower MS River Valley/northern Gulf coast
   through tonight. Cold temperatures aloft attendant to the cyclone
   may support adequate, albeit weak, buoyancy for occasional lightning
   flashes across the Big Bend region of TX and across South TX this
   morning and afternoon. More scattered thunderstorms are expected
   across the lower MS Valley later tonight as ascent through the
   850-500 mb layer increases ahead of the approaching upper wave.
   Given the recent cold frontal passage, convection will be elevated
   in nature. Although effective shear through the CAPE-bearing layer
   may increase to 25-30 knots, saturation through a deep layer with
   nearly moist-adiabatic lapse rates will result in slim buoyancy
   profiles that will act to modulate updraft intensities. (Similar
   thermodynamic conditions were noted in the 00z LIX sounding with
   paltry convection in the vicinity.) Consequently, severe
   thunderstorms are not expected. Elsewhere, more isolated
   thunderstorms are expected along a frontolytic cold front across
   parts of the FL peninsula as well as along portions of the West
   Coast as an upper wave begins to approach the region.

   ..Moore/Dean.. 11/24/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 240646

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1246 AM CST Tue Nov 24 2026

   Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER SOUTHERN
   FLORIDA AND THE KEYS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few strong storms are possible over parts of South Florida
   Wednesday.

   ...Discussion...
   An upper low will move from the central Plains into the Mid South,
   with a negatively tilted upper trough moving across the eastern Gulf
   and FL Wednesday night. Ahead of this trough, surface pressures will
   lower over the FL region, with modest southerly winds during the
   day, and rapidly veering overnight with the passage of the upper
   wave.

   During the day on Wednesday, substantial clouds and precipitation
   are expected, which will limit heating and destabilization. Overall
   instability levels look to be weak, but sufficient given increasing
   lift and low 70s F dewpoints. Cluster of storms developing over the
   eastern Gulf and/or across the FL Straits may impact the Keys and
   far southern FL beginning early in the day, and a few strong to
   severe gusts cannot be ruled out with any larger clusters. The
   tornado risk currently appears low due to predicted weak low-level
   shear.

   ..Jewell.. 11/24/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 240823

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0223 AM CST Tue Nov 24 2026

   Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A deepening upper low is forecast to move northeastward out of the
   Mid South and across the TN and OH Valleys on Thursday, with a
   leading wave ejecting northward across the Mid Atlantic. A surface
   low should develop and move northward just off the coastal Mid
   Atlantic, with a zone of rain and a few thunderstorms shifting out
   of NC and into PA and NJ.

   Instability will likely be limited with the warm frontal surge, as
   widespread precipitation limits heating. This warm advection regime
   in the low levels will also impinge upon a relatively cool air mass
   over land, suggesting the more robust surface-based storms will
   remain largely offshore. 

   Elsewhere, cool temperatures aloft north of a midlevel jet may
   support low-topped convection over coastal Washington with minimal
   instability and shoreline convergence Thursday morning.

   ..Jewell.. 11/24/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
